title: The Short Proposal and Separate Demo
lede: Use your discovery to create a plain proposal you can read together. Open the demo separately.
body:
By this point you know the buyer’s problem and have checked the proposed solution with the delivery team. This lesson turns that into a document you can walk through on the sales call. The buyer should understand what is wrong, what it costs, what changes, when it happens and what they pay.

A document about their business

Default to one readable page where the scope fits. If you need a second page or a scope appendix, use it. Don’t squeeze tiny text onto one page, and don’t turn every heading into a slide.

  • Overview: who the proposal is for, what we are building and why.
  • The problem and impact: what the owner and team told you, the consequences and any agreed cost calculation.
  • Proposed build out: the included work, what it solves, what connects and what people still approve.
  • Timeline: stages, reviews, testing and handover.
  • Costs and next step: approved build price, ongoing costs, payment terms and how to proceed.

No marketing headlines, agency history or embedded demo. Missing numbers stay missing until you confirm them. Time released is not automatically cash saved.

Build the proposal

Run the proposal skill for this prospect using my saved discovery and approved scope. Keep the demo separate.

Read it as the owner. Check every number, deliverable, date and payment term against what was actually agreed. If the scope or price still needs approval, keep it as an internal draft.

Show one useful workflow separately

For a custom build, a short demonstration can make the solution easier to understand. Open it in its own file or tab, then return to the proposal. The proposal can contain a simple link.

Use either a clearly labelled illustrative mock-up with sample data, or a connected test using authorised records. Show one useful job and one realistic exception. A clickable front end is not proof the integrations work.

Using this prospect’s saved solution brief, build a separate short demonstration of one workflow and one exception. Tell me whether it is a mock-up or a connected test. Keep it outside the proposal.

Before the sales call

Can the buyer explain the problem, the change and what they are buying after a quick read? Are scope and costs clear? Does the separate demo work on the screen you will share? Fix those before adding design.
